newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rubber still soft in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rubber still soft in late trade.

text.p: Indonesian tyre-grade SIR20 rubber offer prices continued to be in the doldrums in late trading on Friday as buyers remained absent, traders said.
They said benchmark SIR20 for April/May shipment was still at 52.75 U.S. cents/lb fob Medan and Surabaya, at 52.50 fob Palembang and Jambi and at 52.00 fob Pontianak.
Offer prices were heard at 53.00 cents/lb fob Padang, up from 52.25 in the morning, but no deals were heard.
"There are no deals done today. The problem is there are no buyers coming to the market," said one trader.
Traders said buyers stayed away from the market because they already had enough stock. One trader said they expected to sell at least at 53.00 when buyers started to enter the market again.

"From what I've learned, both U.S. and European buyers are not making any fresh purchases because they have enough stock. Usually, China enters the market this month for June and July shipment, but it has not shown up until now," he said.

Traders said both buyers and sellers were still taking a wait-and-see stance. "We can only hope the price will stay the way it is for next week because it is hard to make predictions in this kind of situation," said one trader.
